title: Multiples of three, plus ten
scenario: Take the multiples of 3 and add 10 to each.

intro.job: Take the multiples of 3 and add 10 to each.

idea.rule: The if in a comprehension picks who gets in — if x % 3 lets in everything that ISN'T a multiple of 3.
idea.detail: [x + 10 for x in nums if CONDITION] is a for loop squeezed onto one line: take each x, let it in only if the condition is True, and put x + 10 in the new list. Read it as: 'x plus 10, for every x in nums, if x is a multiple of 3.' The if decides WHO gets in — so it has to test the right thing.

watch.code:
added = [v + 10 for v in vals if v % 3 == 0]
print(added)

model_restatement: Keep only the multiples of 3, add 10 to each one, and print the new list.

clarify.question: Could there be zero or negative numbers?
clarify.answer: Not today — positive whole numbers only.

clarify.question: Should the result keep the original order?
What if there are no multiples of 3?

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Make a new list: each number plus 10, keeping only the numbers that pass the check. Print it.
draft_code:
out = [x + 10 for x in nums if x % 3]
print(out)

checkpoints.prompt: When the comprehension is done, what is out?
With the fix — what is out?

why_line: if x % 3 is truthy for the non-multiples — 4 and 7 get in, 3 and 6 stay out — exactly backwards.

explain.rule: The bouncer lets in whoever is truthy — and x % 3 is truthy for the non-multiples, so 4 and 7 stroll in and the multiples stay out.
explain.bridge: So what question would only let the multiples of 3 in?

fix.rule: x % 3 == 0 is the multiple-of-3 test: the remainder after dividing by 3 is 0 only for multiples of 3.

walk.gloss: For each x, let it in only if it's a multiple of 3, and put x + 10 in the list.

contrast.wrong_note: truthy for non-multiples — lets the wrong ones in

fix.recommended:
out = [x + 10 for x in nums if x % 3 == 0]
print(out)

alternatives.note: The same thing as a plain loop — four lines instead of one.

hints: What does x % 3 give for 3, 4, 6, 7 — and which of those are truthy?
The if is the filter. You want 'x is a multiple of 3'.

follow_up.recommended:

print(out)
follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — no multiples of 3 in the list, so nothing gets 10 added.

one_liner: The if in a comprehension picks who gets in — if x % 3 lets in everything that ISN'T a multiple of 3.
